pr_title: PR merge improvements: auto-merge, edit commit body
pr_body:
- Adds `pr merge --auto`, `pr merge --disable-auto` modes
- Folds in https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/2896

```
$ gh pr merge --auto --squash 40
✓ Pull request #40 will automatically get merged via squash when all requirements are met

$ gh pr merge --disable-auto 40
✓ Auto-merge disabled for pull request #40
```

Questions:
- The confirmation checkmark for `merge --auto` is green. Should it be purple?
- The confirmation checkmark for `merge --disable-auto` is green. Should it be red?

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/2619
Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/1023
Reverts #1627, reasoning https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/2954#issuecomment-779390768, ref. https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/1621

TODO:
- [x] tests for `--auto`
- [x] tests for `--disable-auto`
- [x] GHE compatibility for `viewerMergeBodyText` GraphQL field

issue_context.title: Support pr auto-merge from gh
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

GitHub recently announced [PR auto-merge](https://github.com/github/roadmap/issues/107) to automatically merge PRs when all checks are passing and the PR is approved with no conflicts.

### Proposed solution

We can support this in GitHub CLI. Here's the proposed design:

`gh pr merge --auto` to enable automerge on a PR.
`gh pr merge --auto-disable` to disable automerge on a PR.

### Additional context

This feature won't be GA until sometime in the next couple months, so we should wait until it's broadly available to ship this in GitHub CLI.
comments: Really need this on `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge`.

I would actually like a setting on the project to where we can enable automerge always from select users (like dependabot where github would merge it for me)

Currently I had to make an automerge workflow in github actions to do that when all of the checks pass.
I think the `auto` option is still missing on `gh pr create` command. Is this supposed to be implemented?
@amansilla No, we've opted to _not_ add the `--auto` flag to `gh pr create`. You may separately enable auto-merge for your new PR with the `gh pr merge --auto` command after running `gh pr create`.
All right @mislav! Thanks for the clarification.

> @amansilla No, we've opted to _not_ add the `--auto` flag to `gh pr create`. You may separately enable auto-merge for your new PR with the `gh pr merge --auto` command after running `gh pr create`.

does that support telling it how it must merge it (like rebase merge for example) too?
@AraHaan Yes; please refer to `gh pr merge` documentation.
When I run `gh pr merge --auto`, it still prompts me for how it should merge. Do I need to always use `gh pr merge --auto --merge`? I'm using this in a CICD.
@CMCDragonkai Yes, you have to explicitly declare a merge strategy.

boo, it's not like git where we can configure ``gh config pr.mergeStrategy commit/squash/rebase`` (which I think would be much better to do to define a default for when one does not explicitly declare it (to use the one from config in that case).

> it's not like git where we can configure `gh config pr.mergeStrategy`

Does git have a configuration option for a default merge strategy? Would you mind pointing it out to me? I can't see it in git help—the option `pr.mergeStrategy` does not exist, which makes sense because git has no concept of "Pull Requests".

We might add a config option in the future, but we will first have to also enable repository-specific config for gh, which we don't have right now. Otherwise, a locally configured default merge strategy will work for some repos but not for others, since GitHub repos can prohibit certain merge strategies in their settings.

In the meantime, feel free to create a gh alias with your favorite merge strategy:
```
gh alias set sq "pr merge --squash"
```

> @amansilla No, we've opted to _not_ add the `--auto` flag to `gh pr create`. You may separately enable auto-merge for your new PR with the `gh pr merge --auto` command after running `gh pr create`.

Please reconsider this decision. Running `gh pr merge --auto` immedately after `gh pr create` sometimes results in the following error:
```
no pull requests found for branch "test-branch"
```

I can avoid detecting the PR number from the branch name by capturing the created PR URL returned by `gh pr create` and providing it as an argument to `gh pr merge`:
```
pr_url="$(gh pr create --fill)"
gh pr merge --auto -r "$pr_url"
```
This is also not reliable, as this sometimes fails with the following error:
```
GraphQL: Could not resolve to a PullRequest with the number of 183. (repository.pullRequest)
```

I suspect that the API used by `gh pr create` returns before the newly created PR is propagated to the entire system. The second command might interact with an API endpoint that does not yet know about the existence of the newly created PR. 
I currently have to resort to a wait and retry mechanism in our CI/CD pipeline as a workaround, but it would be great if this is resolved on the API or CLI side.

To add to this, when a branch has protections requiring a review the `gh pr merge` command fails out with: 
`Message: At least 1 approving review is required by reviewers with write access., Locations: [{Line:1 Column:58}]`

If the gh create had the option, this error would not be thrown because it would not try to merge until the review came in.

Is there another work around? Will we just need to create another workflow to trigger when a review happens?

review_comments: It seems like enabling automerge should also short circuit the flow of the command. What was behind the decision to move that functionality down into the `mergePullRequest` function?

@samcoe Since enabling auto-merges accepts identical inputs as the `mergePullRequest` mutation, I've decided to keep all behaviors of normal `pr merge` intact in `--auto` mode, including the interactive ones.
